codes.unknown_dependency: depends on a service that isn't in this file.
codes.foreign_network: joins a network this project doesn't own. Projects are kept apart, so remove it. To use a database from another project, publish its port on its Expose tab and connect through the server's address.
codes.foreign_image: names an image something else on this server may run, or runs one only another project has. A built image takes the stack's own name: leave image out, or start it with the stack's name.
codes.runs_program: hands work to a program Compose would run on the server itself, outside any container. Opsifier does not run those.
codes.privileged: runs in privileged mode, with full control of the server.
codes.docker_socket: mounts the Docker socket, which gives it control of the server.
codes.data_directory: mounts the panel's own data, including its secrets.
codes.host_path: mounts a folder from the server, or a path only known at deploy time.
codes.host_namespace: shares a namespace with the server or another container.
codes.devices: gets direct access to devices on the server.
codes.container_name: sets container_name, which can clash with another container.
codes.published_port: publishes a port directly on the server, bypassing the proxy.
codes.port_taken: publishes a port something else already uses.
codes.no_restart_policy: has no restart policy, so it stays down after a reboot.
codes.external_resource: reaches a volume or container outside this stack.
codes.profiles: sits behind a profile, so a plain deploy won't start it.
codes.network_mode: uses its own network mode, so domains can't reach it.
codes.unroutable_name: has a name that can't be used as a domain target.

issues.hostTitle: This stack can take over the server
issues.hostBody: Mounting the Docker socket, running privileged or reaching into the server's files gives this stack the power to control the machine. Only confirm if you trust everything it runs.
issues.confirmLabel: I understand and trust this file
issues.adminOnly: Only an administrator can confirm this file.
issues.confirmed: Confirmed for this version of the file
